thought_title: Stay inseparable from Christ and the bishop, for outside the sanctuary no one is clean

edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Φυλάττεσθε οὖν τοὺς τοιούτους. τοῦτο δὲ ἔσται ὑμῖν μὴ φυσιουμένοις καὶ οὖσιν ἀχωρίστοις θεοῦ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου καὶ τῶν διαταγμάτων τῶν ἀποστόλων. [2] ὁ ἐντὸς θυσιαστηρίου ὢν καθαρός ἐστιν: ὁ δὲ ἐκτὸς θυσιαστηρίου ὤν οὐ καθαρός ἐστιν. τοῦτ̓ ἔστιν, ὁ χωρὶς ἐπισκόπου καὶ πρεσβυτερίου καὶ διακόνων πράσσων τι, οὗτος οὐ καθαρός ἐστιν τῇ συνειδήσει.
pass_a_gloss: Guard yourselves, then, against such people. And this will be so for you if you are not puffed up and are inseparable from God, Jesus Christ, and from the bishop and from the ordinances of the apostles. The one who is within the place of the altar is pure; but the one who is outside the place of the altar is not pure. That is, whoever does anything without the bishop and the presbytery and the deacons, this person is not pure in his conscience.
pass_b_english: So be on your guard against such people. And this will hold true for you if you are not puffed up with pride, and if you stay inseparable from God, Jesus Christ, and from the bishop and the commands of the apostles.

Whoever is inside the altar's sanctuary is clean; whoever is outside the sanctuary is not clean. That is, whoever does anything apart from the bishop, the presbytery, and the deacons does not have a clean conscience.

choices.why: θυσιαστήριον here is the altar precinct; 'within the altar' is not English. Ignatius uses it for the gathered church around the altar.
rejected: inside the church (interprets the image away)

choices.why: Lake prints θεοῦ but notes it as doubtful (A omits). English keeps both nouns without adding 'our'.
Ritual-purity image of the altar; 'clean' carries both cultic and moral sense.
rejected: pure (fine; less vivid with the sanctuary image)

choices.why: φυσιόω = puff up; a Pauline word for arrogance.

choices.english: And this will hold true for you
choices.why: τοῦτο stays the subject of ἔσται; no narrower referent supplied.

anf_compare.notes: Sense aligned. ANF 'Jesus Christ our God' adds 'our' to a word Lake marks doubtful; ANF 'within the altar' kept literal.

notes: Lake note at 7.1: θεοῦ doubtful; A omits it; probably some corruption.
φυσιόω is Pauline vocabulary (1 Corinthians 4:6; 8:1) but no specific verse is quoted; not tagged inline.
Repair 2026-10-02 per checker a: one genitive slot 'God, Jesus Christ' (Lake θεοῦ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, θεοῦ marked doubtful); τοῦτο as subject of ἔσται; τι restored.
Repair round 1: τοῦτο restored as subject in Pass B; title now names the thought.

review.notes: Paragraph [1] checked in full. Φυλάττεσθε οὖν τοὺς τοιούτους is the imperative in both A (“Guard yourselves, then, against such people”) and B. τοῦτο δὲ ἔσται ὑμῖν μὴ φυσιουμένοις καὶ οὖσιν ἀχωρίστοις θεοῦ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου καὶ τῶν διαταγμάτων τῶν ἀποστόλων keeps τοῦτο as subject, the negative participle, and inseparability from God, Jesus Christ, the bishop, and the apostles’ διατάγματα (A “ordinances,” B “commands”). Both altar clauses keep ἐντός/ἐκτός and οὐ καθαρός; πράσσων τι … οὐ καθαρός ἐστιν τῇ συνειδήσει is kept, including τι. No quoted scripture, so no inline citation was due; 1 Cor. parallels are marked vocabulary only. Title names the sanctuary/ministry thought, not only the locus.

Source paragraph 1: Locked Greek contains 'Φυλάττεσθε οὖν τοὺς τοιούτους. τοῦτο δὲ ἔσται ὑμῖν μὴ φυσιουμένοις καὶ οὖσιν ἀχωρίστοις θεοῦ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου καὶ τῶν διαταγμάτων τῶν ἀποστόλων.' Pass A renders this as 'Guard yourselves, then, against such people. And this will be so for you if you are not puffed up and are inseparable from God, Jesus Christ, and from the bishop and from the ordinances of the apostles.' Pass B renders it as 'So be on your guard against such people. And that guard will hold for you as long as you are not puffed up with pride and stay inseparable from God, Jesus Christ, and from the bishop and the commands of the apostles.' The Greek phrase 'τοῦτο δὲ ἔσται ὑμῖν' (literally 'this will be for you') is rendered by Pass A as 'And this will be so for you' and by Pass B as 'And that guard will hold for you'. The latter introduces a specific referent 'that guard' (referring back to 'be on your guard') which is not present in the Greek. The Greek 'τοῦτο' refers to the entire condition of being unswollen and inseparable, not specifically to the act of guarding. This adds an interpretation not in the source, violating completeness and agency by narrowing the referent. Additionally, the title 'Inside the sanctuary is clean: nothing apart from bishop, presbytery and deacons' fails to name the thought; it only describes a locus and omits the conditional clause about guarding against such people and being unswollen with pride, thus failing to capture the full thought of the passage. Covered source paragraphs: [1].
reasons: Pass B: 'And that guard will hold for you as long as you are not puffed up with pride...' adds 'that guard' as referent for τοῦτο, which is not in the Greek; Greek τοῦτο refers to the condition of being unswollen and inseparable, not the act of guarding.

Title: 'Inside the sanctuary is clean: nothing apart from bishop, presbytery and deacons' names only a locus, not the thought; omits the conditional warning against puffed-upness and the call to guard against such people.
